executive_assessment.text: Rimac/Lima water dependence, Sierra/Alta Selva farming constraints and modeled district flood exposure describe different vulnerabilities; modeled exposure is not actual damage or a 2026 basin measurement.

Named Puno environmental disputes document governance context without climate attribution. The 2012 Andean competition hypothesis and Canrey Chico account add historically bounded mechanism/capacity evidence, not proven climate-caused violence.

geographic_notes.text: Source dated 2022-11 reports: The report associates El Niño with more flooding on the Costa and drought in the Sierra; agriculture and fisheries’ large employment and export shares add exposure.

Source dated 2023 reports: The report identifies the Rimac Basin as the sharpest deficit: Lima’s 11 million residents rely on Atlantic-region transfers for several months yearly; north-coast irrigated agriculture is also threatened by scarcity.

Source dated 2023 reports: In Sierra and Alta Selva, where half of rural residents are poor, only about 20% of cultivated land is irrigated, leaving farming exposed to rainfall shifts; most Costa agricultural land is irrigated.

Source dated 2025 reports: Under possible summer El Niño/La Niña rainfall anomalies, the plan rates 78 districts across 12 departments very high flood risk, covering 2.396 million people; Annex 4 names Belén and Piura districts including Catacaos and Tambogrande.

Source dated 2025-12 reports: Authorities and residents of Ocuviri and Vila Vila, Puno, demanded environmental remediation of the Hatun Ayllu basin and a plenary session involving ministers and other senior officials.

Source dated 2025-12 reports: The Llallimayo case covers Ayaviri, Cupi, Llalli and Umachiri in Melgar, Puno; an environmental-recovery worktable expired in December 2025 after a 2020 rights action was suspended, and local actors sought a replacement development table.

Source dated 2012-06 reports: Huascarán Park’s head said glacier retreat, warming and erratic rain were weakening Cordillera Blanca wetlands’ and pastures’ water regulation; low-income settlers and illegal miners were entering sensitive highlands exposed to glacial-lake outbursts.
Source dated 2012-06 reports: An interviewed MINAM director said warming-related crop and herder shifts may intensify Andean resource competition.

Source dated 2012-06 reports: Canrey Chico leaders said two decades of learning, a water group and improved farming raised pasture quality and reduced conflict; they reported declining a mining proposal.

known_gaps.text: Automated machine-screening is not independent source verification or human approval. 14 of 14 evidence records and 0 of 0 pathways lack claim-level verification in this remediation; review the linked records before relying on them.
Recent official conflict monitoring gives named cases in Puno and other departments but does not attribute these cases to climate hazards.

The only inspected source explicitly discussing climate-related conflict mechanisms is a 2012 nonofficial, qualitative field discussion paper; its competition pathway is an attributed potential mechanism, not a tested causal finding or proof of violence.

No reverse pathway from current insecurity or conflict to climate-adaptation implementation was established in the inspected evidence; the CCDR's subnational DRM constraints are not attributed to FCV.
The 2025–2027 government plan records intended targets, not verified delivery; national and basin diagnostics cannot substitute for current site-level implementation evidence.
The new bank does not splice current Puno environmental disputes into a climate causal chain. Their primary monitoring source states no climate attribution.
A complete source-supported four-link pathway is not assembled from the 2012 interview hypothesis alone; community-reported capacities are retained separately as qualitative historical evidence.
Draft extension: human source review and approval remain pending. Lending eligibility is not an FCV classification.
